reason: The current goal is to build the bed structure, so placing steel on the growing-room floor seems like a direct start.
expectation: I expect the steel to form a bed frame or support, though further fittings will probably be needed.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hose to the reservoir looks useful for irrigation, but the bed structure is the immediate goal.

effect: The raised frames establish separate crop beds with outlets above the future reservoir; they still need lining and irrigation.
reaction: The different bed depths are a satisfying, practical detail.
reason: Line the raised frames to continue building the shared beds.
expectation: I expect the food-safe sheet to line the beds, though drainage fittings may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The hose and pump will likely serve irrigation, but lining the frames seems the more direct next step.

effect: The beds now hold solution and have sealed drain fittings; they still need plumbing to the reservoir.
reaction: Sealing around the drains is a sensible detail.
reason: Connect the hose to the reservoir and pump to prepare the irrigation system.
expectation: I expect a hose-equipped reservoir and pump that can then connect to the beds.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hose to the beds first also seems useful, but I prefer preparing the reservoir connection.

effect: The reservoir now has a pump and an aerating return, ready to sit beneath the beds.
reaction: The falling return stream mixing air into the solution is a useful detail.
reason: The only offered gameplay action connects hose to the lined beds, advancing the irrigation setup.
expectation: I expect the hose to provide plumbing for the beds, though it may not complete the connection to the reservoir yet.

effect: The beds now drain toward the reservoir, and the next goal is to complete the aerated return.
reaction: The gravity-fed drains make practical sense.
reason: The only gameplay option joins the prepared reservoir and drained beds, directly addressing the new goal.
expectation: I expect a connected recirculating bed and reservoir system, though it may still need water or other fittings.

effect: The reservoir and beds now form a shared distribution system with separate root-zone adjustments; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The shared system with individual flow controls is a satisfying practical detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the aerating reservoir was most worthwhile: the falling return stream explains how the solution gains air before recirculation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the bed drains was sensible but less engaging, especially as it was the only gameplay option offered.

surprise.text: The beds have different depths and flow adjustments for the three crops, rather than being identical sections of one bed.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the lining, drainage and reservoir connections each had a clear physical purpose.

continue.text: Yes. The physically explained irrigation details make me curious to see how the growing system is put to use, although the forced choices were less engaging.
